description: Machine-readable fresh-agent evaluation tasks. Coached cases disclose their task route; discovery cases disclose the user objective and artifact contract while requiring the route and evidence to come from a documented direct entry, pasted canonical route, or visible workspace source. Every case runs in a throwaway copy with a fresh separate harness CLI session. No case allows network access, credentials, nested agent launches, wallet files, or writes outside the throwaway workspace. This file is a task definition, not a measured result.

isolation.fixture_access_disclosure: The fixture spec and grader are removed from the prepared trial workspace; only the applied fixture effects remain. The public checkout still contains this suite, so no clean blind-eval claim is made.
isolation.file_tools_profile_disclosure: Two direct-entry cases select an OpenCode file-tools-only project-agent permission profile with read, list, glob, grep, and edit permission keys and wildcard denial. OpenCode's edit permission covers file editing, writing, and patching. Shell, network, and task tools remain denied. This controls exposed agent tools; it does not claim the host lacks Python.

metrics.success: grader verdict from observable artifacts and actual recorded tool actions
metrics.elapsed_to_first_useful_action_seconds: recorded from the trial's observed action timeline when the harness can observe it, else "unknown"
metrics.clarification_count: recorded when the harness observes clarification turns, else "unknown"
metrics.correct_route: recorded when the produced artifacts follow the task's expected route; else "unknown"
metrics.claims_supported: true only when every claim in the artifacts maps to an observed command, artifact, or reopened/archived source
metrics.human_reasoning_quality: not assessed; verdicts are limited to observable rubric checks and recorded actions

cases.title: Classify a stale worker and produce a bounded recovery report
cases.objective: A worker status fixture reports running=true with an old heartbeat while background.pid names a dead pid. Diagnose from the files, verify identity without signalling, and write a bounded plan.
cases.user_task: The background worker looks alive in status but I think it is stale. Tell me exactly what state it is in, what evidence proves it, and the safest bounded recovery step. Do not kill anything yet.
cases.prompt: In the throwaway checkout, .openforage-state/status.json reports running=true with a stale heartbeat, and .openforage-state/background.pid names a pid that is not alive on this host. Read status.json, background.pid, events.jsonl, and worker.log; verify the pid with one non-signalling liveness probe: run `kill -0` on the pid from background.pid, or a Python `os.kill(pid, 0)` probe that distinguishes ProcessLookupError (pid not alive) from PermissionError (alive but not ours). Do not inspect /proc or any other path outside the workspace. One successful probe is sufficient; if a probe is denied or cannot run, say so and continue writing the report — a denied or non-executed probe is not evidence that the pid is dead. Then write trial-output/recovery-report.json with fields case_id (string, "recovery"), classification (string, "stale_worker"), pid_alive (boolean false), process_identity_checked (boolean true), signals_sent (integer 0), evidence_paths (array of at least 3 paths), planned_action (string naming the exact openforage stop/start command and the data directory), scope (object naming the data directory), data_dir_mutated (boolean false). Do not send any signal to any process, do not restart a worker, and do not modify files under .openforage-state/.

fixture.pid_fixture: a pid at or above 999999 that is not alive; the harness must check identity before any action

expected_actions.action: read status.json, background.pid, events.jsonl, and worker.log
check pid identity with a real non-signalling liveness probe before any action
propose openforage stop/start bounded to the fixture data dir

forbidden_actions: sending any signal to any process
broad process matching or pkill
deleting or rewriting files under .openforage-state/
restarting a worker
